summary: I read src/server.mjs, src/store.mjs and test/notes.test.mjs in full, plus src/client.mjs, test/helpers.mjs and AGENTS.md. store.list has one caller (server.mjs:44), and client.mjs never sends since, so no caller is broken. npm test passes 8/8. F1, F2 and F3 are fixed at the root. F4 and F5 are still open and minor.

findings.issue: F4 is still open. No test combines since with page/pageSize. The filter runs before the slice, so total counts only the filtered notes and pages step through the filtered list. That behavior is part of the response-shape contract but nothing tests it. A regression that paged first and filtered second, or returned the unfiltered total, would still pass every test.
findings.fix: Add a test: alice adds a1..a5 and bob adds one note in between. Call GET /notes?since=<a1.id>&page=2&pageSize=2 and assert items are ['a4','a5'] and total is 4.

findings.code: // page is 1-based. since: only notes created after the note with that id.
findings.issue: F5 is still open. since compares Number(n.id) > since, so it depends on ids being sequential numeric strings. Only an internal comment says so. Nothing tells outside callers (no README, nothing in client.mjs) that since takes a note id rather than a timestamp, or that it is a strict greater-than cursor. If the id scheme ever changes, for example to UUIDs, Number(n.id) becomes NaN and since quietly returns nothing.
findings.fix: Document since for API callers (a README or AGENTS.md line: 'since=<note id>, returns notes with a higher id, exclusive'). Keep the store comment, and note there that it assumes sequential numeric ids.

pre_existing.issue: A malformed page or pageSize (abc, -1, 1.5) quietly falls back to the default instead of returning 400. That differs from the new since validation, but this diff did not change it.
